BEARISH_FLAG.name: Bearish Flag
BEARISH_FLAG.description: A chart pattern formed by a strong downward price move (pole) followed by a brief, narrow upward-sloping consolidation channel (flag). It indicates a brief pause in selling pressure before the previous downward trend resumes.
BEARISH_FLAG.conditions: Established strong downtrend (pole) followed by an ascending parallel consolidation channel with lower volume.
BEARISH_FLAG.entry: On a confirmed candle close below the lower trendline of the flag.
BEARISH_FLAG.target: Height of the flagpole measured downwards from the breakdown point.
BEARISH_FLAG.stop_loss: Placed above the upper trendline of the flag pattern.

RISING_WEDGE.name: Rising Wedge
RISING_WEDGE.description: A chart pattern formed by two upward-sloping, converging trendlines where higher lows rise faster than higher highs. It indicates that bullish momentum is losing strength as price range contracts, leading to an eventual downside breakout.
RISING_WEDGE.conditions: Prior uptrend, price creating higher highs and higher lows within converging ascending trendlines.
RISING_WEDGE.entry: Below the lower trendline upon breakdown with a confirmed candle close.
RISING_WEDGE.target: Height of the widest part of the wedge measured downwards from the breakdown point.
RISING_WEDGE.stop_loss: Just above the most recent high inside the wedge.

TRIPLE_TOP.name: Triple Top
TRIPLE_TOP.description: A pattern forming after an uptrend, where the price makes three distinct highs at approximately the same level, separated by two interim troughs (neckline). This indicates a strong resistance level and potential reversal to a downtrend.
TRIPLE_TOP.conditions: Preceded by a clear uptrend. The three peaks should be relatively equal in price, and volume typically increases on the breakdown below the neckline.
TRIPLE_TOP.entry: Enter short once the price breaks decisively below the neckline (the lows between the tops).
TRIPLE_TOP.target: The price target is typically the height of the pattern (from the highest top to the neckline) projected downwards from the breakdown point.
TRIPLE_TOP.stop_loss: Place the stop-loss order above the neckline or slightly above the third top.

BULLISH_SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.name: Bullish Symmetrical Triangle
BULLISH_SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.description: This pattern is formed by a series of contracting price ranges, creating converging trendlines. It suggests a pause in the uptrend before the price continues higher.
BULLISH_SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.entry: After the price breaks decisively above the upper trendline.
BULLISH_SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.target: The height of the triangle projected upwards from the breakout point.
BULLISH_SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.stop_loss: Placed below the lower trendline of the triangle.

BEARISH_SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.name: Bearish Symmetrical Triangle
BEARISH_SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.description: This pattern is characterized by converging trendlines, indicating a temporary consolidation in a downtrend before the price moves lower.
BEARISH_SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.entry: After the price breaks decisively below the lower trendline.
BEARISH_SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.target: The height of the triangle projected downwards from the breakout point.
BEARISH_SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.stop_loss: Placed above the upper trendline of the triangle.

CUP_&_HANDLE.name: Cup & Handle
CUP_&_HANDLE.description: A classic chart pattern featuring a rounded U-shaped cup followed by a small downward consolidation forming the handle. It reflects a temporary pause in a bullish trend before buyers regain control and push the price upward through resistance.
CUP_&_HANDLE.conditions: An established prior uptrend, formation of a smooth rounded cup bottom, followed by a smaller handle consolidation with decreasing volume.
CUP_&_HANDLE.entry: On a confirmed breakout above the horizontal resistance line (rim) after the handle completes.
CUP_&_HANDLE.target: Equal to the depth of the cup (distance from resistance rim to cup bottom) projected upward from the breakout level.
CUP_&_HANDLE.stop_loss: Placed just below the lowest point of the handle.

INVERTED_CUP_&_HANDLE.name: Inverted Cup & Handle
INVERTED_CUP_&_HANDLE.description: This pattern is the inverse of the Cup & Handle, featuring a rounded top (inverted cup) followed by a downward-sloping handle. It suggests a potential bearish reversal and continuation of the downtrend.
INVERTED_CUP_&_HANDLE.conditions: Usually follows an uptrend. The "inverted cup" is a rounding top, and the "handle" is a short-term bounce.
INVERTED_CUP_&_HANDLE.entry: After the price breaks below the support level of the handle.
INVERTED_CUP_&_HANDLE.target: The depth of the inverted cup projected downwards from the breakout point of the handle.
INVERTED_CUP_&_HANDLE.stop_loss: Placed above the high of the handle or the top of the inverted cup.

ASCENDING_TRIANGLE.name: Ascending Triangle
ASCENDING_TRIANGLE.description: A consolidation pattern characterized by a horizontal upper resistance line and a rising lower support line that forms higher lows. It indicates increasing buying pressure as buyers continuously step in at higher price levels until a breakout occurs.
ASCENDING_TRIANGLE.conditions: Existing uptrend leading into the pattern, a flat resistance ceiling with at least two touches, and a series of higher lows forming a rising support trendline.
ASCENDING_TRIANGLE.entry: Upon a confirmed breakout above the flat resistance line, ideally accompanied by strong volume.
ASCENDING_TRIANGLE.target: Equal to the maximum height of the triangle projected upward from the breakout point.
ASCENDING_TRIANGLE.stop_loss: Placed just below the most recent higher low inside the triangle or below the rising support line.

DESCENDING_TRIANGLE.name: Descending Triangle
DESCENDING_TRIANGLE.description: A chart pattern featuring a flat horizontal support level and a downward-sloping resistance line. It indicates increasing selling pressure as each consecutive rally peaks lower than the previous one before breaking below support.
DESCENDING_TRIANGLE.conditions: Existing downtrend with price consolidating between a horizontal support line and a falling resistance trendline.
DESCENDING_TRIANGLE.entry: On a firm breakdown below the flat support line with high volume confirmation.
DESCENDING_TRIANGLE.target: Subtract the maximum vertical height of the triangle from the breakdown point.
DESCENDING_TRIANGLE.stop_loss: Above the high of the breakdown candle inside the triangle.

BULLISH_RECTANGLE.name: Bullish Rectangle
BULLISH_RECTANGLE.description: This pattern is characterized by a period of consolidation between two parallel horizontal lines. It suggests a pause in the uptrend before it continues.
BULLISH_RECTANGLE.conditions: The market should be in an uptrend prior to the rectangle formation.
BULLISH_RECTANGLE.entry: Upon a decisive breakout above the upper horizontal resistance line, preferably with high volume.
BULLISH_RECTANGLE.target: The height of the rectangle added to the breakout price.
BULLISH_RECTANGLE.stop_loss: Placed below the lower horizontal support line of the rectangle.

BEARISH_RECTANGLE.name: Bearish Rectangle
BEARISH_RECTANGLE.description: This pattern represents a period of consolidation in a downtrend, bounded by two parallel horizontal lines. It signifies a pause before the downtrend resumes.
BEARISH_RECTANGLE.conditions: The market should be in a downtrend prior to the rectangle formation.
BEARISH_RECTANGLE.entry: Upon a decisive breakdown below the lower horizontal support line, preferably with high volume.
BEARISH_RECTANGLE.target: The height of the rectangle subtracted from the breakout price.
BEARISH_RECTANGLE.stop_loss: Placed above the upper horizontal resistance line of the rectangle.

THREE_WHITE_SOLDIERS.name: Three White Soldiers
THREE_WHITE_SOLDIERS.description: A three-candlestick pattern consisting of three consecutive long bullish (green) candles, each opening within the body of the previous candle and closing higher than the previous candle, with small or no wicks. It signals strong and sustained buying pressure.
THREE_WHITE_SOLDIERS.conditions: Can appear after a downtrend (reversal) or during an uptrend (continuation). Each candle should ideally open within the previous body and close near its high.
THREE_WHITE_SOLDIERS.entry: Enter on the close of the third bullish candle or on the open of the next candle if momentum continues.
THREE_WHITE_SOLDIERS.target: Previous significant resistance levels or a measure of the preceding downtrend for a reversal.
THREE_WHITE_SOLDIERS.stop_loss: Below the low of the second candle, or conservatively below the low of the first candle.

THREE_OUTSIDE_DOWN.name: Three Outside Down
THREE_OUTSIDE_DOWN.description: A three-candlestick pattern indicating a strong bearish reversal. It starts with a small bullish (green) candle, followed by a large bearish (red) candle that completely engulfs the first candle (Bearish Engulfing), and is confirmed by a third bearish candle that closes below the low of the second candle.
THREE_OUTSIDE_DOWN.conditions: Appears after an uptrend. First candle bullish, second bearish (engulfing the first), third bearish closing below the second's low.
THREE_OUTSIDE_DOWN.entry: Enter short on the open of the fourth candle, or when the third candle closes below the low of the second candle.
THREE_OUTSIDE_DOWN.target: Nearest significant support level or previous swing lows.
THREE_OUTSIDE_DOWN.stop_loss: Above the high of the second (engulfing) candle.

BEARISH_ENGULFING.name: Bearish Engulfing
BEARISH_ENGULFING.description: A two-candlestick pattern where a small bullish candle is completely engulfed by a larger bearish candle that follows it. It signifies a strong shift in market sentiment from buying pressure to selling pressure, overcoming previous bullish momentum.
BEARISH_ENGULFING.conditions: Must occur after a clear uptrend. The body of the second (bearish) candle must fully cover the body of the first (bullish) candle.
BEARISH_ENGULFING.entry: Enter after the bearish engulfing candle closes, or on the open of the next candle.
BEARISH_ENGULFING.target: Expect a move towards the next significant support level.
BEARISH_ENGULFING.stop_loss: Place the stop-loss order above the high of the second (engulfing) candle.

DARK_CLOUD_COVER.name: Dark Cloud Cover
DARK_CLOUD_COVER.description: A long bullish candle (green) is followed by a long bearish candle (red). The bearish candle opens above the high of the previous bullish candle and closes more than halfway into the body of the bullish candle.
DARK_CLOUD_COVER.conditions: Must appear after a distinct uptrend. The bearish candle's close must be below the midpoint of the preceding bullish candle's body.
DARK_CLOUD_COVER.entry: Enter after the close of the second (bearish) candle or on the open of the next candle, upon confirmation of downward movement. The image suggests entry below the low of the second candle.
DARK_CLOUD_COVER.target: The next significant support level or prior swing low.
DARK_CLOUD_COVER.stop_loss: Place the stop-loss above the high of the second (bearish) candle or the highest point of the pattern.

THREE_BLACK_CROWS.name: Three Black Crows
THREE_BLACK_CROWS.description: Composed of three consecutive long bearish candles that open within the previous candle's real body and close progressively lower, often with small or no lower wicks. Each candle shows strong selling pressure.
THREE_BLACK_CROWS.conditions: Forms after a clear uptrend, indicating a strong reversal and the beginning of a new downtrend. Increased volume on each candle enhances reliability.
THREE_BLACK_CROWS.entry: Enter short after the close of the third bearish candle, or on the open of the next candle if momentum is strong.
THREE_BLACK_CROWS.target: A significant downward move, targeting the next support level or a measured move based on the prior uptrend.
THREE_BLACK_CROWS.stop_loss: Above the high of the first (or highest) candle in the pattern, or above the high of the third candle for a tighter stop.

THREE_OUT_SIDE_DOWN.name: Three Out Side Down
THREE_OUT_SIDE_DOWN.description: This pattern signals a strong bearish reversal after an uptrend. It starts with a bullish candle, followed by a larger bearish candle that completely engulfs the first one, forming a bearish engulfing pattern. A third bearish candle closes lower than the second, confirming the downward trend.
THREE_OUT_SIDE_DOWN.conditions: Appears in a clear uptrend. The second bearish candle must entirely engulf the body and potentially the range of the first bullish candle.
THREE_OUT_SIDE_DOWN.entry: Enter a short position after the close of the third bearish candle, or on the open of the subsequent candle.
THREE_OUT_SIDE_DOWN.target: An initial target could be the nearest significant support level, anticipating a sustained downtrend.
THREE_OUT_SIDE_DOWN.stop_loss: Place the stop-loss order above the high of the second (engulfing) candle.

BEARISH_LONG_LEGGED_DOJI.name: Bearish Long Legged Doji
BEARISH_LONG_LEGGED_DOJI.description: A Doji candle with very long upper and lower shadows, and a small real body typically near the middle. When it appears after an uptrend, it signals strong indecision but can precede a bearish reversal.
BEARISH_LONG_LEGGED_DOJI.conditions: Appears at the top of an uptrend, indicating strong contention between buyers and sellers after a sustained rally. Requires confirmation by a subsequent bearish candle.
BEARISH_LONG_LEGGED_DOJI.entry: Enter below the low of the Long Legged Doji or the low of the next bearish confirmation candle.
BEARISH_LONG_LEGGED_DOJI.target: Target previous support levels or a 1:2 risk-reward ratio from the entry to stop-loss distance.
BEARISH_LONG_LEGGED_DOJI.stop_loss: Above the highest point of the Long Legged Doji's upper shadow.

BEARISH_SPINNING_TOP.name: Bearish Spinning Top
BEARISH_SPINNING_TOP.description: A single candlestick with a small real body and long upper and lower shadows of roughly equal length. Indicates indecision between buyers and sellers.
BEARISH_SPINNING_TOP.conditions: Appears after a clear uptrend, signaling that the bulls might be losing momentum and a potential reversal to a downtrend.
BEARISH_SPINNING_TOP.entry: Enter short below the low of the Spinning Top, or on the close of a strong bearish candle confirming the reversal.
BEARISH_SPINNING_TOP.target: A move equivalent to at least the height of the pattern, or to the next significant support level.
BEARISH_SPINNING_TOP.stop_loss: Place the stop-loss order above the high of the Bearish Spinning Top candlestick.

FALLING_THREE_METHOD.name: Falling Three Method
FALLING_THREE_METHOD.description: A five-candle pattern consisting of a long bearish candle, followed by three small-bodied bullish candles that stay within the range of the first, and ending with a final long bearish candle closing below the first's close.
FALLING_THREE_METHOD.conditions: Occurs within an established downtrend, with the three small candles showing minor rebound but failing to close above the first bearish candle's high.
FALLING_THREE_METHOD.entry: Enter short after the close of the fifth (final) strong bearish candle, confirming the resumption of the downtrend.
FALLING_THREE_METHOD.target: A continuation of the previous downtrend's momentum, potentially to new lows or support levels.
FALLING_THREE_METHOD.stop_loss: Place the stop-loss above the high of the three small bullish candles, or above the high of the first long bearish candle.

BULLISH_KICKER.name: Bullish Kicker
BULLISH_KICKER.description: This pattern is formed by a bearish candle followed by a bullish candle that gaps above the previous bearish candle's high. It suggests a strong shift in momentum from bearish to bullish.
BULLISH_KICKER.conditions: The market should be in a downtrend.
BULLISH_KICKER.entry: Enter long on the close of the bullish kicker candle.
BULLISH_KICKER.target: The target is usually the gap size measured move.
BULLISH_KICKER.stop_loss: Place the stop-loss below the low of the kicker candle.

BEARISH_KICKER.name: Bearish Kicker
BEARISH_KICKER.description: This pattern consists of a bullish candle followed by a bearish candle that gaps below the previous bullish candle's low. It indicates a potential reversal from an uptrend to a downtrend.
BEARISH_KICKER.conditions: The market should be in an uptrend.
BEARISH_KICKER.entry: Enter short on the close of the bearish kicker candle.
BEARISH_KICKER.target: The target is the gap size measured move.
BEARISH_KICKER.stop_loss: Place the stop-loss above the high of the kicker candle.

TWEEZER_BOTTOM.name: Tweezer Bottom
TWEEZER_BOTTOM.description: This pattern is formed by two consecutive candlesticks with identical or very close lows. It typically occurs at the end of a downtrend and suggests that selling pressure is weakening.
TWEEZER_BOTTOM.conditions: Appears during a downtrend. The first candle is bearish (red), and the second is bullish (green) or doji, and their lows align perfectly or very closely.
TWEEZER_BOTTOM.entry: Enter a long position after the second candle closes, or on the confirmation of an upward move.
TWEEZER_BOTTOM.target: Expected move is upwards, usually aiming for a significant resistance level or a measured move.
TWEEZER_BOTTOM.stop_loss: Place the stop-loss just below the low of the tweezer bottom.

TWEEZER_TOP.name: Tweezer Top
TWEEZER_TOP.description: This pattern consists of two consecutive candlesticks with identical or very close highs. It usually forms at the end of an uptrend and indicates that buying pressure is faltering.
TWEEZER_TOP.conditions: Occurs during an uptrend. The first candle is bullish (green), and the second is bearish (red) or doji, and their highs align perfectly or very closely.
TWEEZER_TOP.entry: Enter a short position after the second candle closes, or upon confirmation of a downward move.
TWEEZER_TOP.target: Expected move is downwards, often targeting a significant support level or a measured move.
TWEEZER_TOP.stop_loss: Place the stop-loss just above the high of the tweezer top.

BEARISH_DIAMOND_TOP.name: Bearish Diamond Top
BEARISH_DIAMOND_TOP.description: This is a rare bearish reversal pattern, appearing at the end of an uptrend. Price action initially widens, then narrows, forming a distinct diamond shape. It signals a potential downward price movement.
BEARISH_DIAMOND_TOP.conditions: Forms after a prolonged uptrend, indicating exhaustion of buying pressure. Confirmation by increasing volume on breakout is preferred.
BEARISH_DIAMOND_TOP.entry: Initiate a short position upon a confirmed breakout below the diamond's lower right trendline.
BEARISH_DIAMOND_TOP.target: Measure the maximum height of the diamond and project it from the breakout level.
BEARISH_DIAMOND_TOP.stop_loss: Place above the highest swing high within the diamond pattern.

DOUBLE_BOTTOM.name: Double Bottom
DOUBLE_BOTTOM.description: A classic "W" shaped pattern where price touches a support level twice without breaking below it, creating two distinct bottoms with a peak in between. It signifies a shift in momentum from sellers to buyers as the price defends a strong support zone.
DOUBLE_BOTTOM.conditions: Prior downtrend, two distinct troughs reaching approximately the same price level, separated by a interim peak (neckline).
DOUBLE_BOTTOM.entry: When the price breaks and closes above the middle resistance (neckline) level.
DOUBLE_BOTTOM.target: Equal to the vertical height between the bottom support level and the neckline, projected upward from the breakout point.
DOUBLE_BOTTOM.stop_loss: Placed just below the lowest low of the two bottoms.

DOUBLE_TOP.name: Double Top
DOUBLE_TOP.description: A major bearish reversal pattern characterized by two distinct peaks at nearly the same price level, resembling an "M" shape. It indicates strong resistance and price rejection at key highs, signaling a shift from bullish to bearish control.
DOUBLE_TOP.conditions: Must form after an established uptrend, with price failing twice to breach a specific resistance level before breaking key support.
DOUBLE_TOP.entry: Enter short when the price breaks and closes below the intermediate support/neckline.
DOUBLE_TOP.target: Measure the vertical distance from the top resistance level to the support neckline, and project that distance downwards from the breakdown point.
DOUBLE_TOP.stop_loss: Placed slightly above the high of the two resistance peaks.

TRIPLE_BOTTOM.name: Triple Bottom
TRIPLE_BOTTOM.description: A pattern forming after a downtrend, where the price makes three distinct lows at approximately the same level, separated by two interim peaks (neckline). This indicates a strong support level and potential reversal to an uptrend.
TRIPLE_BOTTOM.conditions: Preceded by a clear downtrend. The three bottoms should be relatively equal in price, and volume typically increases on the breakout above the neckline.
TRIPLE_BOTTOM.entry: Enter long once the price breaks decisively above the neckline (the highs between the bottoms).
TRIPLE_BOTTOM.target: The price target is typically the height of the pattern (from the lowest bottom to the neckline) projected upwards from the breakout point.
TRIPLE_BOTTOM.stop_loss: Place the stop-loss order below the neckline or slightly below the third bottom.

BULLISH_PENNANT.name: Bullish Pennant
BULLISH_PENNANT.description: A continuation pattern forming after a sharp upward move (pole). It's a small symmetrical triangle consolidation, indicating a brief pause before the prior uptrend resumes.
BULLISH_PENNANT.conditions: Preceded by a strong uptrend; volume typically decreases during formation and increases on breakout.
BULLISH_PENNANT.entry: Enter long upon a confirmed breakout above the upper trendline of the pennant.
BULLISH_PENNANT.target: Measure the length of the 'pole' and project it upwards from the breakout point.
BULLISH_PENNANT.stop_loss: Place below the lowest point of the pennant or just below the lower trendline.

BEARISH_PENNANT.name: Bearish Pennant
BEARISH_PENNANT.description: A continuation pattern forming after a sharp downward move (pole). It's a small symmetrical triangle consolidation, indicating a brief pause before the prior downtrend resumes.
BEARISH_PENNANT.conditions: Preceded by a strong downtrend; volume typically decreases during formation and increases on breakout.
BEARISH_PENNANT.entry: Enter short upon a confirmed breakout below the lower trendline of the pennant.
BEARISH_PENNANT.target: Measure the length of the 'pole' and project it downwards from the breakout point.
BEARISH_PENNANT.stop_loss: Place above the highest point of the pennant or just above the upper trendline.

BULLISH_FLAG.name: Bullish Flag
BULLISH_FLAG.description: A continuation pattern following a sharp upward move (pole). It consists of two parallel, downward-sloping trendlines, representing a temporary consolidation before the uptrend continues.
BULLISH_FLAG.conditions: Occurs within an existing strong uptrend; volume typically subsides during formation and spikes on breakout.
BULLISH_FLAG.entry: Enter long upon a confirmed breakout above the upper trendline of the flag.
BULLISH_FLAG.target: Measure the length of the 'pole' and project it upwards from the breakout point.
BULLISH_FLAG.stop_loss: Place below the lowest point of the flag or just below the lower trendline.

ORDER_BLOCKS.name: Order Blocks
ORDER_BLOCKS.description: An Order Block is a specific price range where institutions or "smart money" entered large positions. A bullish order block forms after a strong upward move and indicates potential buying pressure. A bearish order block forms after a strong downward move and indicates potential selling pressure.
ORDER_BLOCKS.conditions: Occurs after a strong, impulsive move. The block itself is typically a single candle or a small cluster of candles with a visible imbalance.
ORDER_BLOCKS.entry: For a bullish order block, enter on a retest of the block's area after price has moved away from it. For a bearish order block, enter on a retest after price has moved away.
ORDER_BLOCKS.target: The target is the next significant resistance or support level, or a continuation of the prior trend.
ORDER_BLOCKS.stop_loss: For a bullish order block, place the stop loss below the low of the order block. For a bearish order block, place the stop loss above the high of the order block.

FAIR_VALUE_GAPS_(FVG).name: Fair Value Gaps (FVG)
FAIR_VALUE_GAPS_(FVG).description: A Fair Value Gap is a price inefficiency where there is a significant gap between three or more candlesticks. Bullish FVGs indicate potential buying support, while bearish FVGs indicate potential selling resistance.
FAIR_VALUE_GAPS_(FVG).conditions: Occurs during strong, unidirectional price movements where price quickly moves away from the initial candlestick, leaving a void.
FAIR_VALUE_GAPS_(FVG).entry: Enter when price returns to fill the FVG. A bullish FVG suggests buying as price enters the gap, and a bearish FVG suggests selling as price enters the gap.
FAIR_VALUE_GAPS_(FVG).target: The target is typically the opposite end of the previous impulsive move or the next significant area of liquidity.
FAIR_VALUE_GAPS_(FVG).stop_loss: For a bullish FVG, place the stop loss below the FVG. For a bearish FVG, place the stop loss above the FVG.

BREAK_OF_STRUCTURE_(BOS).name: Break of Structure (BOS)
BREAK_OF_STRUCTURE_(BOS).description: A BOS occurs when price breaks through a significant swing high (in an uptrend) or swing low (in a downtrend). This confirms that the existing trend is likely to continue.
BREAK_OF_STRUCTURE_(BOS).conditions: Must be occurring within an established trend, breaking a previous structural high or low.
BREAK_OF_STRUCTURE_(BOS).entry: Enter after the structure has been broken and price has retested the broken structure level, confirming it as support or resistance.
BREAK_OF_STRUCTURE_(BOS).target: The next major swing level or liquidity pool.
BREAK_OF_STRUCTURE_(BOS).stop_loss: Place the stop-loss below the last swing low for a long entry, or above the last swing high for a short entry.

LIQUIDITY_SWEEPS.name: Liquidity Sweeps
LIQUIDITY_SWEEPS.description: A liquidity sweep occurs when price aggressively moves to take out buy-side or sell-side liquidity (stops placed above swing highs or below swing lows) before reversing. This often indicates a trap for retail traders.
LIQUIDITY_SWEEPS.conditions: Price moves significantly beyond a previous swing high or low, indicating a potential stop hunt, and then reverses sharply, often with high volume.
LIQUIDITY_SWEEPS.entry: For a bullish liquidity sweep, enter long after price has taken out sell-side liquidity and begins to move upwards, ideally with confirmation from other SMC concepts. For a bearish liquidity sweep, enter short after price has taken out buy-side liquidity and begins to move downwards.
LIQUIDITY_SWEEPS.target: The target is typically the opposite side of the range where the sweep occurred, or the next significant inefficiency.
LIQUIDITY_SWEEPS.stop_loss: For a bullish sweep, place the stop loss below the low of the sweep candle or the area of new demand. For a bearish sweep, place the stop loss above the high of the sweep candle or the area of new supply.

STANDARD_DOJI_(INDECISION).name: Standard Doji (Indecision)
STANDARD_DOJI_(INDECISION).description: The Standard Doji is characterized by having an open and close price that are almost the same, with long upper and lower wicks. This pattern indicates that neither buyers nor sellers were able to gain control during the trading period, leading to market indecision.
STANDARD_DOJI_(INDECISION).conditions: Appears after a strong trend (uptrend or downtrend).
STANDARD_DOJI_(INDECISION).entry: After the confirmation of the next candle, in the direction indicated by the Doji's context.
STANDARD_DOJI_(INDECISION).stop_loss: Slightly above the high or below the low of the Doji candle.

ABANDONED_BABY_(BULLISH).name: Abandoned Baby (Bullish)
ABANDONED_BABY_(BULLISH).description: This is a rare but highly reliable bullish reversal pattern. It consists of a downtrend followed by a gap-down Doji, and then a gap-up strong bullish candle. The three candles are isolated, meaning they do not overlap with each other.
ABANDONED_BABY_(BULLISH).entry: After the confirmation of the third (bullish) candle closing.
ABANDONED_BABY_(BULLISH).target: Expected to be a significant upward move, often continuing the previous trend's magnitude in reverse.
ABANDONED_BABY_(BULLISH).stop_loss: Below the low of the Doji or the lowest point of the pattern.

ABANDONED_BABY_(BEARISH).name: Abandoned Baby (Bearish)
ABANDONED_BABY_(BEARISH).description: This is a three-candle pattern. It consists of a strong bullish candle, followed by a doji that gaps away from the first candle, and then a strong bearish candle that gaps away from the doji.
ABANDONED_BABY_(BEARISH).entry: After the third bearish candle closes.

THREE_LINE_STRIKE_(BULLISH).name: Three Line Strike (Bullish)
THREE_LINE_STRIKE_(BULLISH).description: This pattern is characterized by three consecutive rising candles, followed by a large bearish candle that erases all previous gains. Despite its appearance, it often acts as a bullish continuation pattern.
THREE_LINE_STRIKE_(BULLISH).conditions: The market should be in an uptrend, but showing signs of consolidation or short-term exhaustion.
THREE_LINE_STRIKE_(BULLISH).entry: Enter long on the next candle after the large bearish candle, expecting it to continue upwards.
THREE_LINE_STRIKE_(BULLISH).target: The target is an upward move, often to new highs.
THREE_LINE_STRIKE_(BULLISH).stop_loss: Place the stop-loss below the low of the large bearish candle.

BULLISH_BELT_HOLD.name: Bullish Belt Hold
BULLISH_BELT_HOLD.description: This pattern consists of a long bullish candle that opens at its low and closes near its high, indicating strong buying pressure. It appears after a downtrend and signals a potential reversal.
BULLISH_BELT_HOLD.entry: On the confirmation candle (the 5th candle) closing above the prior candle's high.
BULLISH_BELT_HOLD.target: The height of the pattern (from the low of the Belt Hold candle to its close) projected upwards.
BULLISH_BELT_HOLD.stop_loss: Below the low of the Belt Hold candle.

MAT_HOLD_(CONTINUATION).name: Mat Hold (Continuation)
MAT_HOLD_(CONTINUATION).description: This pattern features a strong upward move followed by three small bearish (or neutral) candles that do not significantly retrace the prior gains. This is followed by a strong bullish candle, indicating a continuation of the uptrend.
MAT_HOLD_(CONTINUATION).conditions: Follows a strong bullish move. The pullback candles are small and do not erase previous gains.
MAT_HOLD_(CONTINUATION).entry: After the breakout candle (the final strong bullish candle) closes.
MAT_HOLD_(CONTINUATION).target: The previous resistance level or an upward projection based on the preceding bullish move.
MAT_HOLD_(CONTINUATION).stop_loss: Below the low of the final breakout candle or below the lows of the small pullback candles.

RISING_THREE_METHODS.name: Rising Three Methods
RISING_THREE_METHODS.description: This pattern consists of a long bullish candle followed by three small bearish candles, which are contained within the range of the first candle. It is then followed by another long bullish candle that closes above the first one, indicating that the uptrend is likely to continue.
RISING_THREE_METHODS.entry: Entry is on the close of the fifth candle (the final long bullish candle).
RISING_THREE_METHODS.target: The target is calculated by taking the height of the first bullish candle and adding it to the closing price of the fifth candle.
RISING_THREE_METHODS.stop_loss: A stop-loss can be placed below the low of the fourth candle (the last small bearish candle).

TRI-STAR_PATTERN.name: Tri-Star Pattern
TRI-STAR_PATTERN.description: This is a rare but powerful bullish reversal pattern formed by three consecutive doji candles. The middle doji is the smallest, and the first and third doji are typically larger, indicating a significant shift in market sentiment.
TRI-STAR_PATTERN.entry: Entry is on the close of the confirmation candle following the third doji.
TRI-STAR_PATTERN.target: The target is the previous swing high level.
TRI-STAR_PATTERN.stop_loss: The stop-loss is placed below the doji cluster.

ROUNDING_BOTTOM_(SAUCER).name: Rounding Bottom (Saucer)
ROUNDING_BOTTOM_(SAUCER).description: This pattern represents a long-term accumulation phase, characterized by a gradual U-shaped recovery after a downtrend. It indicates a shift in sentiment from selling to buying.
ROUNDING_BOTTOM_(SAUCER).conditions: Occurs after a significant downtrend. The shape is slow, gradual, and smooth, resembling a saucer.
ROUNDING_BOTTOM_(SAUCER).entry: After a breakout above the resistance level.
ROUNDING_BOTTOM_(SAUCER).target: The depth of the pattern added to the breakout point.
ROUNDING_BOTTOM_(SAUCER).stop_loss: Below the lowest point of the pattern.

ROUNDING_TOP.name: Rounding Top
ROUNDING_TOP.description: This pattern signifies a long-term topping process and distribution phase after an uptrend. It suggests that selling pressure is gradually increasing.
ROUNDING_TOP.conditions: Occurs after a significant uptrend. The shape is an inverted U, also known as an inverted saucer.
ROUNDING_TOP.entry: After a breakdown below the support level.
ROUNDING_TOP.target: The depth of the pattern subtracted from the breakdown point.
ROUNDING_TOP.stop_loss: Above the highest point of the pattern.

DIAMOND_TOP.name: Diamond Top
DIAMOND_TOP.description: This pattern is characterized by widening price ranges that then contract into a diamond shape at the market top. It indicates increasing volatility followed by a period of contraction, often preceding a significant price decline.
DIAMOND_TOP.conditions: Occurs at market tops, suggesting exhaustion of an uptrend.
DIAMOND_TOP.entry: On a breakdown below the lower trendline of the diamond formation.
DIAMOND_TOP.target: The height of the widest part of the diamond formation, projected downwards from the breakdown point.
DIAMOND_TOP.stop_loss: Placed above the recent high within the diamond formation.

DIAMOND_BOTTOM.name: Diamond Bottom
DIAMOND_BOTTOM.description: This pattern is the mirror image of the Diamond Top, forming at market bottoms. It signifies initial volatility expansion followed by contraction, suggesting a potential reversal from a downtrend to an uptrend.
DIAMOND_BOTTOM.conditions: Occurs at market bottoms, indicating potential exhaustion of a downtrend.
DIAMOND_BOTTOM.entry: On a breakout above the upper trendline of the diamond formation.
DIAMOND_BOTTOM.target: The height of the widest part of the diamond formation, projected upwards from the breakout point.
DIAMOND_BOTTOM.stop_loss: Placed below the recent low within the diamond formation.

BROADENING_PATTERN_(MEGAPHONE).name: Broadening Pattern (Megaphone)
BROADENING_PATTERN_(MEGAPHONE).description: This pattern is characterized by diverging trendlines, where both higher highs and higher lows are expanding. It indicates increasing volatility and market indecision.
BROADENING_PATTERN_(MEGAPHONE).entry: After a clear breakout in either direction.
BROADENING_PATTERN_(MEGAPHONE).stop_loss: Beyond the opposite side of the pattern.

ASCENDING_CHANNEL.name: Ascending Channel
ASCENDING_CHANNEL.description: The Ascending Channel is formed by two parallel up-sloping trendlines, with price moving within these boundaries. It represents a bullish continuation pattern where the asset is in an uptrend.
ASCENDING_CHANNEL.conditions: The price is moving between two parallel up-sloping trendlines.
ASCENDING_CHANNEL.target: Expected to continue within the channel.

DESCENDING_CHANNEL.name: Descending Channel
DESCENDING_CHANNEL.description: This pattern is characterized by two parallel downward-sloping trendlines, with the price moving within them. It suggests a bearish continuation, where the downtrend is expected to persist.
DESCENDING_CHANNEL.conditions: The market must be in a clear downtrend, and the price should be contained within two parallel descending trendlines.
DESCENDING_CHANNEL.entry: Enter a short position near the upper trendline of the channel or upon a breakdown below the channel.
DESCENDING_CHANNEL.target: The lower trendline of the channel or a measured move of the channel's width.
DESCENDING_CHANNEL.stop_loss: Above the upper trendline of the channel.

ISLAND_REVERSAL.name: Island Reversal
ISLAND_REVERSAL.type: Bullish / Bearish (depending on the direction of the initial trend)
ISLAND_REVERSAL.description: This pattern occurs when a price gap is followed by another gap in the opposite direction, creating an "island" of price action isolated from the rest of the chart. It signals a potential reversal of the current trend.
ISLAND_REVERSAL.conditions: Requires two price gaps in opposite directions, with the price action between these gaps forming an "island." It is often seen after significant news or liquidation events in volatile markets like crypto.
ISLAND_REVERSAL.entry: After the second gap confirms the reversal.
ISLAND_REVERSAL.stop_loss: On the opposite side of the "island."

WOLFE_WAVE.name: Wolfe Wave
WOLFE_WAVE.description: A 5-point chart pattern that forms a channel, often with a distorted shape. It suggests a reversal when wave 5 returns to the ETA line (formed by points 1-3). It's an advanced pattern requiring practice to identify effectively.
WOLFE_WAVE.conditions: A 5-point structure where price forms a channel. Wave 5 should break out and return to the ETA line.
WOLFE_WAVE.entry: After wave 5 completes and returns towards the ETA line.
WOLFE_WAVE.target: The ETA line (which can be extended from points 1-3).

THREE_DRIVES_PATTERN.name: Three Drives Pattern
THREE_DRIVES_PATTERN.type: Bullish / Bearish (depending on the direction of the drives)
THREE_DRIVES_PATTERN.description: This pattern consists of three symmetrical extension drives, often based on Fibonacci sequences, that signal an exhaustion reversal. The price makes three distinct moves in the same direction, with pullbacks in between.
THREE_DRIVES_PATTERN.conditions: Three successive price drives in the same direction, with pullbacks between each drive. The pattern suggests exhaustion after multiple attempts to move in one direction.
THREE_DRIVES_PATTERN.entry: After the completion of the third drive and confirmation of a reversal.
THREE_DRIVES_PATTERN.target: Based on Fibonacci extensions from the drives or the overall pattern structure.
THREE_DRIVES_PATTERN.stop_loss: Placed beyond the extreme of the third drive.

THREE_SYMMETRIC_PRICE_'DRIVES'.name: Three Symmetric Price 'Drives'
THREE_SYMMETRIC_PRICE_'DRIVES'.type: Bullish / Bearish (depending on the direction of the drives)
THREE_SYMMETRIC_PRICE_'DRIVES'.description: This pattern involves three successive price movements, or "drives," which are measured using Fibonacci extensions (127%/161.8%). It signifies exhaustion after a prolonged trend.
THREE_SYMMETRIC_PRICE_'DRIVES'.conditions: The pattern is based on the completion of the third drive and subsequent retracement. It is also related to Elliott Wave and Harmonic patterns.
THREE_SYMMETRIC_PRICE_'DRIVES'.entry: After the third drive is complete and a retracement is confirmed.
THREE_SYMMETRIC_PRICE_'DRIVES'.target: The starting point of the first drive.
THREE_SYMMETRIC_PRICE_'DRIVES'.stop_loss: Beyond the extreme of the third drive.

BULLISH_ORDER_BLOCK_(SUPPORT_ZONE).name: Bullish Order Block (Support Zone)
BULLISH_ORDER_BLOCK_(SUPPORT_ZONE).description: This pattern signifies a potential bullish reversal. It is identified by a last down-candle before a strong impulsive up-move, which acts as a support zone. Institutions and large traders are believed to place their orders in this zone.
BULLISH_ORDER_BLOCK_(SUPPORT_ZONE).conditions: Occurs after a downtrend or consolidation, followed by a strong bullish impulse move. The price should then retrace back to this zone.
BULLISH_ORDER_BLOCK_(SUPPORT_ZONE).entry: Enter on the retest of the Order Block zone, confirmed by a bullish candle.
BULLISH_ORDER_BLOCK_(SUPPORT_ZONE).stop_loss: Slightly below the Order Block zone.

FAIR_VALUE_GAP_(FVG)_/_IMBALANCE.name: Fair Value Gap (FVG) / Imbalance
FAIR_VALUE_GAP_(FVG)_/_IMBALANCE.description: This pattern represents a price inefficiency where the gap between the high of the first candle and the low of the third candle is not filled by the second candle. It suggests that the price is likely to return to fill this gap.
FAIR_VALUE_GAP_(FVG)_/_IMBALANCE.conditions: A three-candle structure where the middle candle is strong, and there's a gap between the high of the first candle and the low of the third candle.
FAIR_VALUE_GAP_(FVG)_/_IMBALANCE.entry: Enter when the price approaches to fill the Fair Value Gap.
FAIR_VALUE_GAP_(FVG)_/_IMBALANCE.target: The price will typically fill the gap.

FV_G_FILL_KE_BAAD_PRICE_CONTINUATION.name: FV G fill ke baad price continuation
FV_G_FILL_KE_BAAD_PRICE_CONTINUATION.description: After an FV G (Fair Value Gap) is filled, the price tends to continue in the same direction as the prevailing trend. This pattern indicates strength in the existing trend.
FV_G_FILL_KE_BAAD_PRICE_CONTINUATION.conditions: A clear trend must be present, and the price must have previously created an FVG which is now being filled.
FV_G_FILL_KE_BAAD_PRICE_CONTINUATION.entry: Enter when price returns to the FVG zone and shows a reaction confirming the direction of the trend.
FV_G_FILL_KE_BAAD_PRICE_CONTINUATION.target: The next significant liquidity or swing level.
FV_G_FILL_KE_BAAD_PRICE_CONTINUATION.stop_loss: Place the stop-loss below the FVG zone for a long trade, or above for a short trade.

CHANGE_OF_CHARACTER_(CHOCH).name: Change of Character (CHOCH)
CHANGE_OF_CHARACTER_(CHOCH).description: A CHOCH is the first sign of a potential trend reversal. It occurs when price breaks the structure of the previous trend in the opposite direction, indicating a shift in market sentiment.
CHANGE_OF_CHARACTER_(CHOCH).conditions: Occurs at the end of a trend, where price breaks a significant swing low in an uptrend or swing high in a downtrend.
CHANGE_OF_CHARACTER_(CHOCH).entry: Enter after the CHOCH confirmation, ideally on a retest of the newly formed structure or an associated FVG/Order Block.
CHANGE_OF_CHARACTER_(CHOCH).target: Aim for a significant move in the new direction, potentially targeting previous swing levels or liquidity.
CHANGE_OF_CHARACTER_(CHOCH).stop_loss: Place the stop-loss beyond the last swing high (for a reversal from uptrend to downtrend) or last swing low (for a reversal from downtrend to uptrend).

LIQUIDITY_SWEEP_(STOP_HUNT).name: Liquidity Sweep (Stop Hunt)
LIQUIDITY_SWEEP_(STOP_HUNT).description: This pattern involves price briefly moving below a key support level or above a key resistance level to trigger stop-loss orders (liquidity). The price then sharply reverses in the opposite direction.
LIQUIDITY_SWEEP_(STOP_HUNT).conditions: Price must be approaching a significant support or resistance level where many stop-loss orders are expected to be placed.
LIQUIDITY_SWEEP_(STOP_HUNT).entry: Enter on the sharp reversal after the liquidity sweep, confirming the directional shift.
LIQUIDITY_SWEEP_(STOP_HUNT).target: Target a significant move in the direction of the reversal, often to the opposite side of the previous range or to new structural levels.
LIQUIDITY_SWEEP_(STOP_HUNT).stop_loss: Place the stop-loss below the low of the sweep (for a bullish reversal) or above the high of the sweep (for a bearish reversal).

REVERSAL_TRAP_(FAKEOUT).name: Reversal Trap (Fakeout)
REVERSAL_TRAP_(FAKEOUT).description: A fakeout occurs when price breaks a key level, inducing traders to enter in the direction of the breakout. However, the price quickly reverses, trapping those traders and moving in the opposite direction.
REVERSAL_TRAP_(FAKEOUT).conditions: Price breaks a significant support or resistance level, but fails to sustain the move and reverses sharply.
REVERSAL_TRAP_(FAKEOUT).entry: Enter on the strong reversal candle or pattern that forms after the failed breakout, in the opposite direction of the fakeout.
REVERSAL_TRAP_(FAKEOUT).target: Target a significant move against the fakeout direction, often back towards the original level or beyond.
REVERSAL_TRAP_(FAKEOUT).stop_loss: Place the stop-loss beyond the extreme of the fakeout (e.g., below the low of a false bullish breakout or above the high of a false bearish breakout).

LIQUIDITY_GRAB_WITH_REVERSAL_CANDLE.name: Liquidity Grab with Reversal Candle
LIQUIDITY_GRAB_WITH_REVERSAL_CANDLE.description: This pattern occurs when the price takes out stops (liquidity) with a wick, then closes with a strong reversal candle. This indicates a potential shift in market sentiment.
LIQUIDITY_GRAB_WITH_REVERSAL_CANDLE.conditions: The price should be at a key support or resistance level. The "liquidity grab" wick should be pronounced.
LIQUIDITY_GRAB_WITH_REVERSAL_CANDLE.entry: Enter after the reversal candle closes.
LIQUIDITY_GRAB_WITH_REVERSAL_CANDLE.target: The opposite side of the recent swing level.
LIQUIDITY_GRAB_WITH_REVERSAL_CANDLE.stop_loss: Below the extreme wick of the liquidity grab.

HEAD_&_SHOULDERS.name: Head & Shoulders
HEAD_&_SHOULDERS.description: A classic technical analysis pattern featuring three peaks, where the middle peak (head) is the highest and the two surrounding peaks (shoulders) are lower and roughly equal in height. It signals that a prevailing uptrend is losing momentum and about to reverse downward.
HEAD_&_SHOULDERS.conditions: Existing uptrend, clear formation of a left shoulder, higher head, and lower right shoulder, accompanied by a defined neckline support level.
HEAD_&_SHOULDERS.entry: Enter a short position after a candle closes below the neckline support line.
HEAD_&_SHOULDERS.target: Vertical distance from the top of the head down to the neckline, projected downward from the neckline breakout point.
HEAD_&_SHOULDERS.stop_loss: Slightly above the high of the right shoulder.

INVERSE_HEAD_&_SHOULDERS.name: Inverse Head & Shoulders
INVERSE_HEAD_&_SHOULDERS.description: A reliable reversal pattern consisting of three troughs, with the central trough (head) being the deepest and the two flanking troughs (shoulders) being shallower. It marks the end of a downtrend and the start of a bullish trend.
INVERSE_HEAD_&_SHOULDERS.conditions: Existing downtrend, creation of three distinct troughs (left shoulder, head, right shoulder), and a clear neckline resistance level.
INVERSE_HEAD_&_SHOULDERS.entry: Enter a long position after a candle closes above the neckline resistance line.
INVERSE_HEAD_&_SHOULDERS.target: Vertical distance from the bottom of the head up to the neckline, projected upward from the neckline breakout point.
INVERSE_HEAD_&_SHOULDERS.stop_loss: Slightly below the low of the right shoulder.

INVERSE_HEAD_AND_SHOULDERS.name: Inverse Head and Shoulders
INVERSE_HEAD_AND_SHOULDERS.description: A classic bullish reversal pattern featuring three distinct troughs where the central trough (head) is the deepest, flanked by two shallower troughs (shoulders). It signals that selling momentum is exhausting and a new uptrend is beginning as buyers break above the neckline resistance.
INVERSE_HEAD_AND_SHOULDERS.conditions: Must form after an established downtrend; requires increased volume during the breakout above the neckline to confirm validity.
INVERSE_HEAD_AND_SHOULDERS.entry: Enter long after a candle closes above the neckline resistance level.
INVERSE_HEAD_AND_SHOULDERS.target: Measure the vertical distance from the lowest point of the head to the neckline, and project that distance upwards from the breakout point.
INVERSE_HEAD_AND_SHOULDERS.stop_loss: Placed slightly below the low of the right shoulder.

SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.name: Symmetrical Triangle
SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.description: A consolidation pattern formed by lower highs and higher lows converging towards a central point. It reflects a state of temporary market indecision where neither buyers nor sellers hold clear control until a breakout occurs.
SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.conditions: Prior active trend followed by converging support and resistance trendlines forming lower highs and higher lows.
SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.entry: Upon a clear breakout above the upper resistance line (long) or breakdown below the lower support line (short).
SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.target: Project the widest vertical height of the triangle from the breakout or breakdown point.
SYMMETRICAL_TRIANGLE.stop_loss: Placed on the opposite side of the breakout candle or inside the triangle.

BULL_FLAG.name: Bull Flag
BULL_FLAG.description: A strong, sharp upward price move (the pole) followed by a brief consolidation phase within a downward-sloping parallel channel (the flag). It represents a temporary pause before buyers resume driving the price higher in the direction of the original trend.
BULL_FLAG.conditions: Strong preceding uptrend (sharp rise), declining volume during the flag consolidation, and high volume on the upside breakout.
BULL_FLAG.entry: On a confirmed candle close above the upper trendline of the flag.
BULL_FLAG.target: Equal to the height of the pole added to the breakout point.
BULL_FLAG.stop_loss: Just below the lower trendline/lowest point of the flag channel.

BEAR_FLAG.name: Bear Flag
BEAR_FLAG.description: A steep price decline (the pole) followed by a short upward-sloping consolidation channel (the flag). It indicates a brief pause in a downtrend where sellers regain control to push prices further down.
BEAR_FLAG.conditions: Strong preceding downtrend (sharp fall), lower volume during the upward flag phase, and a sharp volume increase upon breakdown.
BEAR_FLAG.entry: On a confirmed candle close below the lower trendline of the flag channel.
BEAR_FLAG.target: Equal to the height of the pole subtracted from the breakdown point.
BEAR_FLAG.stop_loss: Just above the upper trendline/highest point of the flag channel.

PENNANT.name: Pennant
PENNANT.description: A continuation pattern characterized by a sharp initial move (pole) followed by a small symmetrical triangle (pennant) formed by converging trendlines. Price consolidates briefly before breaking out sharply in the direction of the prior trend.
PENNANT.conditions: Strong initial price move (pole) followed by brief consolidation with narrowing price range and declining volume.
PENNANT.entry: On a confirmed breakout outside the pennant trendlines in the direction of the original move.
PENNANT.target: Height of the flagpole added to (or subtracted from) the breakout point.
PENNANT.stop_loss: Placed on the opposite side of the pennant structure.

FALLING_WEDGE.name: Falling Wedge
FALLING_WEDGE.description: A chart pattern characterized by two downward-sloping, converging trendlines where lower highs fall faster than lower lows. It reflects weakening selling pressure as price consolidates, often resolving in a strong upside movement.
FALLING_WEDGE.conditions: Prior downtrend or pullback, price creating lower highs and lower lows within converging descending trendlines.
FALLING_WEDGE.entry: Above the upper trendline upon breakout with a confirmed candle close.
FALLING_WEDGE.target: Height of the widest part of the wedge measured upwards from the breakout point.
FALLING_WEDGE.stop_loss: Just below the most recent low inside the wedge.
